population.note: FICTIONAL. One-line arithmetic: of the 18.8 pts on in 2030, 55% (10.3) stayed on and 8.5 stopped; the off pool of 7.7 + 8.5 = 16.2 restarted at 50% (8.1); 5.5 pts of new ever-users split 4.1 on and 1.4 off; on = 10.3 + 8.1 + 4.1 = 22.5, off = 8.1 + 1.4 = 9.5 = ever 32.0 − current 22.5; cycled = 8.9 prior + ~4.0 first-time restarters = 12.9 of 32.0 ≈ 40%. Persistence rose from ~50% to 55% because generic semaglutide removed price-driven stops. The restart rate fell from 55% to 50% because of deliberate opt-outs tied to the backlash. Users ≈ 22.5% × ~269M adults ≈ 60.5M. Age bands weighted 20/33/24/23% give 2.4 + 7.9 + 8.6 + 3.6 = 22.5. Income thirds average (27 + 23 + 17.5)/3 = 22.5. Bottom-third use rose 4.5 pts, the largest gain, because $39–69 generic semaglutide at chain and discount pharmacies replaced compounded pens and rationed courses. The top third grew least: it was near saturation, and the 'unmedicated' framing caught on fastest there. The 9.5% of adults (~25.6M) who used and are off now include ~3.8M who say in surveys that they stopped for 'natural', religious or body-acceptance reasons (FICTIONAL survey estimate), plus people stopped by the cessation 2×90-day cap, by waiver lockouts or by GI intolerance. About 182M adults have never used. For a growing minority that is a stated position, not a matter of price. Pediatric: ~1.0% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 730k, ~120k of them aged 6–11. Generic price pulled this up and parental opt-out pledges in church and homeschool networks held it down. The oldest adolescent cohorts have ~9 years of exposure, and there is still no bone-accrual readout.

access.public_coverage: Structure unchanged. The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge was extended on identical terms through 2033 in the Dec 2031 health-extenders package: it pays up to $275/month with a $50 copay and the same criteria and DEXA/strength counselling visit for 65+. Since Jan 2032 generic semaglutide fills are reimbursed at pharmacy acquisition cost plus dispensing, under the existing 'lesser-of' clause. About 2.8M Bridge obesity users: ~60% on generic semaglutide at ~$70 average reimbursement and ~40% on tirzepatide or brand at $275 gives a blended $152/month. 2.8M × $152 × 12 ≈ $5.1B/yr run-rate, down from $7.6B with 0.5M more users. Medicare overall pays ≈16.5% of incretin fills ≈ 10.0M users (9.6M adults 65+ = 15.5% × ~62M, plus ~0.4M disabled under-65). Medicaid pays ≈11% ≈ 6.7M users at a blended ~$140 (generic-first PDLs in most states): 6.7M × $140 × 12 ≈ $11.3B/yr combined federal and state. The Indiana and Arkansas waivers are unchanged. The three additional state waiver applications are still pending at CMS, with no action. The HRSA Community Incretin Access Program was flat-funded at $4.5B in FY2031 and FY2032 under continuing resolutions. HRSA used existing contract authority to switch cessation and AUD semaglutide to generic from Feb 2032. FY2032 figures: 2.4M liraglutide × $85 × 12 = $2.45B; 1.6M semaglutide at a blended FY average of $105 (brand $199 for Oct–Jan, generic $60 contract thereafter) × 12 = $2.0B; total ≈ $4.45B against the $4.5B appropriation, for ≈4.0M users. Gambling disorder is not among the programme's statutory purposes, so HRSA does not fund it.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 90+ semaglutide brands at $6–40/month. Generic tirzepatide launched in India, Brazil and Turkey in 2031–32 at $25–60/month. Generic oral semaglutide is sold in ~180 countries. Retatrutide is not generic anywhere.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~60.5M users: commercial 34% (20.6M), Medicare 16.5% (10.0M), Medicaid 11% (6.7M), HRSA free provision 6.6% (4.0M), cash/direct 22.4% (13.6M), gray 9.5% (5.7M) = 100%, 60.6M ≈ 60.5M. Price collapse: generic injectable semaglutide (ANDA entrants plus a Novo authorised generic, launched Jan 2032) sells for $39–69/month cash by Q3 2032. Lilly cut the tirzepatide cash-portal price from $449 to $279 and Foundayo starter doses to $99. Wegovy's list price is still $1,349 for the brand, which is now mostly prescribed for gambling disorder under its exclusive label. Retatrutide still lists at $1,499 and remains allocated. Employer coverage for weight management drifted from 57% to 59%, almost entirely through generic-only tiers. No plan design changed structurally. Pharmacy trend for incretins fell from ~+14% to ~+3% as generic substitution offset higher volume. The gray market halved from 9.0M to 5.7M because $49 legal generic undercut $129–249 compounded vials. What remains is research-peptide retatrutide in gyms (~2.5M), Indian mail pens bought out of habit or distrust of US pharmacies (~1.8M) and 503A 'microdose' sellers (~1.4M). Access is now an income-floor question: the barrier at the bottom is a pharmacy visit, a $49 monthly charge and a prescription, not the price of the molecule.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic brand, plus US generics and Novo authorised generic since Jan 2032)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. US generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, Apr 2029)
gambling disorder (brand semaglutide, Mar 2032; 3-year new-indication exclusivity, carved out of generic labels)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: generic semaglutide for gambling disorder, prescribed around the brand's carved-out indication
compulsive buying, gaming/screen compulsion and compulsive sexual behaviour, citing the gambling trial as rationale
'quiet' and 'focus' low-dose subscriptions, now mostly generic-based at $59–129/month and marketed more cautiously
'metabolic health' longevity regimens with DEXA and strength coaching in the top income third
semaglutide for ages 6–11 under pediatric endocrinology
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class reached the US market (driver: none). MariTide (BLA Jul 2030) had its review extended by a major amendment and received a complete response letter in Oct 2031. The letter asked for 104-week bone-density and body-composition data and a human-factors study of the monthly autoinjector. Amgen plans to resubmit in 2033. Survodutide's resubmission is under review, with an advisory committee in Oct 2032 and a PDUFA date in Feb 2033. Novo held the amycretin resubmission until its North Carolina fill-finish site cleared reinspection in Jun 2032, which puts the decision in 2033. Bimagrumab combinations are still in phase 3. The compulsion driver was realised as a supplement to an existing molecule: brand semaglutide for gambling disorder (sNDA Jul 2031, priority review, approved Mar 2032) on two 26-week trials using a gambling-symptom scale. Compulsive buying and screen compulsion are not DSM diagnoses and were never filed. The US incretin market by revenue fell for the first time, to ≈$120B globally in 2032 (FICTIONAL estimate), as US semaglutide generic erosion outran volume growth and tirzepatide price cuts.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Rates among former gray-market users fell as they moved to pharmacy generics with standard titration.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained. Generic labels match the reference listed drug.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Delayed gastric emptying on drug is established. Persistence after discontinuation is still disputed. MDL 3094 passed ~55,000 filed and tolled claims. Under Mensing preemption, claims against generic makers are largely barred, so plaintiffs concentrate on Novo and Lilly.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The second and third bellwethers split (one defence verdict, Sep 2031; one plaintiff verdict, Apr 2032). No global settlement. FDA still declines a persistent-gastroparesis label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Absolute numbers keep rising with volume and research-peptide retatrutide.
No causal confirmation; low absolute risk. About 7,500 claims inside the MDL.
Still a population problem in 65+. The cheap-generic cohort, mostly unmonitored and low-protein, is the fastest-growing at-risk group.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The class label update (2028) stands. The Bridge extension kept the counselling visit. HRSA and cash generic channels have no body-composition requirement.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: HR ~1.3–1.4 in 65+ long-term and cycling users, concentrated in women. Pediatric bone-accrual data are still absent. The FDA cited this gap in the MariTide CRL.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DEXA recommended in 65+ and postmenopausal women. The pediatric bone-accrual study is ongoing, with an interim readout not before 2033.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; very low absolute risk.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare'; FDA warnings mention unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association. The gambling-disorder trials, run in a population at high psychiatric risk, showed no imbalance.

The 2031 retatrutide postmarketing report found a small, dose-dependent mean shift on a validated anhedonia scale, with a clinically meaningful shift in ~6% at top doses. Surveys still put reduced pleasure at ~10–15% of long-term users. The gambling approval made the mechanism the point of the indication.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No label change. FDA called the data 'consistent with the known pharmacology' and asked for longer follow-up. FTC warning letters continue against 'calm/focus' marketing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Price-driven stops fell. Structural stops (cessation 2×90-day cap, waiver lockouts) and deliberate ideological stops now dominate.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation ongoing; no federal rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Signals for iron, B12, vitamin D and protein insufficiency persist in older and low-income users. Volume in these groups grew with the generic.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of adult follow-up and nine of adolescent. ~120k children aged 6–11 on drug. The pediatric registry's first descriptive report (2032) gave enrolment and adherence figures only.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements and pediatric registry continue.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Poison-centre incretin calls fell ~30% from the 2030 peak as compounded semaglutide vials were displaced by generic pens. Research-peptide retatrutide calls did not fall.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning letters and import alerts continue; still no prosecution of individuals.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent; more often reported in research-peptide users.

food_and_beverage.state: Volume losses continue but are now concentrated in the value channel: dollar stores, discount grocers and the private-label snacks and sugary drinks that bottom-third households bought most. Majors finish divesting indulgent brands to private-equity buyers who target non-users and the 'unmedicated'. A small 'real food, no pharma' premium segment (whole-milk, heritage-grain, 'church-supper' branding) grows from a low base.

alcohol.state: Spirits and beer volumes fall a third consecutive time as cheap generic semaglutide reaches heavy drinkers outside AUD coverage. Non-alcoholic lines and premium single-serve formats grow. Craft breweries in the Upper Midwest consolidate. Tobacco declines continue at the same pace.

restaurants.state: Value-volume chains keep closing units, now in lower-income zip codes as well as mid-income suburbs. Protein-forward fast casual and tasting-menu formats hold. A few Southern buffet chains report steady traffic from church groups and 'unmedicated' diners, a niche, not a turnaround.

apparel.state: Size runs stay wide. Athletic-cut tailoring remains the growth segment. Plus-size stabilises for the first time since 2025, helped by a fat-acceptance revival brand cluster in Oakland and Portland that sells 'heavy on purpose' as identity.

fitness.state: Strength-and-DEXA studios keep expanding. Low-cost gyms gain generic users. Gym-floor research retatrutide persists. Church-basement and 'natural discipline' fasting-and-walking groups compete for the same January customers.

insurance.state: Structurally unchanged. Generic substitution cut incretin pharmacy trend to ~+3%. Plans welcome the gambling-disorder parity obligation once they find they can steer it to generic semaglutide. Adherence gating persists on cessation and AUD benefits.

pharma.state: Novo's US semaglutide revenue roughly halves on generic entry and its authorised generic, and the gambling brand label is a small offset. Lilly's tirzepatide and retatrutide grow in volume at lower net prices. US ANDA holders and Indian API suppliers win volume on thin margins. US sports-betting operators cite 'clinical headwinds' on earnings calls after the gambling approval.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: With the molecule at $49, being on it no longer marks money. Finish still does: muscle, bone and a monitored dose read as top-third. A new, legible third signal has appeared. A heavier body worn deliberately, sometimes with a small cross pin or a 'Full Plate' patch, reads as a statement rather than a failure of access.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: 'The Charlotte build' persists in finance. The bottom-third gap now concerns monitoring, protein and muscle more than use. A visible counter-class has formed: affluent 'unmedicated' parents in Austin and Nashville, and fat-acceptance activists in Oakland, both treating abstention as status.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Smaller portions are still the norm. In Tulsa, a network of about 140 congregations runs 'Daniel Fast' seasons and full Sunday potlucks as explicit alternatives to 'the pharmacy fast'. Family tables mix generic-semaglutide parents, liraglutide children and an abstaining grandparent.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles state molecule and stance: 'on generic', 'reta', 'unmedicated'. Stance mismatches now end more relationships than appetite mismatches. 'Natural' is a dating filter in some apps' religious verticals.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is still a clinical variable for most people. For a loud minority it is a moral or spiritual faculty that a pill steals. The Southern Baptist Convention's 2031 resolution and fat-acceptance writing reach the same conclusion from opposite directions.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Reduced-pleasure reports hold at ~10–15% of long-term users. The 2031 retatrutide data showed a small dose-dependent shift, ~6% clinically meaningful at top doses. Cheap generics made self-titration easy, and surveys put about a third of long-term users on a deliberately reduced or skipped-week schedule (FICTIONAL estimate). 'Focus' subscription users fell from ~1.5–2M to ~1.2M as brands lost novelty and drew complaints. Most are inside the cash share.
interior_life.framing: A complaint with a vocabulary. 'The grey' is everyday speech. 'Skip week' and 'holiday dose' are routine pharmacist questions. Clinicians still say 'reward modulation'. Churches call it 'the dulling'. Gambling-disorder clinicians call it 'the therapeutic effect', and patients sometimes disagree.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Several large employers quietly dropped 'focus' perks after staff complaints and two union grievances that framed them as pressure. DOT apnea clearance still ties some drivers to tirzepatide. Sales and creative staff schedule skip weeks around pitches. HR manuals now include 'dose holiday' as a reason category for performance variance.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' work has moved from novelty to genre, and its novelty is fading. Church worship bands and fat-acceptance zines both claim 'feeling everything' as their aesthetic. Sports-betting handle is softer in high-uptake states. Casinos in Shreveport–Bossier and Atlantic City report lower slot coin-in among locals.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples negotiate skip weeks around anniversaries and holidays as a matter of course. Sex therapists treat dose-timing as standard intake. Partners of gambling-disorder patients describe relief and distance in the same sentence.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: In the 2032 campaign, candidates are asked 'on or off'. Several primary candidates run explicitly 'unmedicated', and one Senate nominee in Oklahoma made it a stump line. The gambling approval drew a joint letter from the betting industry and a coalition of pastors questioning 'medicating vice', allies of convenience. No measured turnout effect.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access on indications, through the gambling-disorder approval, and cautious on new classes (MariTide CRL; survodutide and amycretin pushed to 2033). Enforcement against the remaining gray market is unchanged and symbolic. The FTC still polices 'calm/focus' claims.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No new state action. The HRSA programme is flat-funded at $4.5B under continuing resolutions and still needs annual renewal. The Medicare Bridge was extended unchanged through 2033. The ACA cessation mandate (2×90-day courses) and mental-health parity apply as before, and parity now also reaches gambling disorder. There is no mandate to take the drug.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The Indiana and Arkansas waivers are unchanged: ≥80% PDC, quarterly verified weigh-ins and a 12-month lockout after two misses. The three pending applications are unacted on. HRSA sites still require only refill pickup. At $49 cash, some locked-out Indiana enrollees simply buy generic, which plaintiffs cite to argue the lockout serves no clinical purpose.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT apnea screening, the Army recruit policy and the VA's AUD adoption are all unchanged.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The Section 232 tariff rule covers branded and patented products, and generics are exempt. Indian-made generic semaglutide therefore enters through legal ANDA channels at scale, and Indian API now underpins both the legal generic market and the residual gray market. India's mail-order exports have dropped as a trade-talk item.

events.event: Southern Baptist Convention adopts a resolution 'On Appetite, Discipline and the Pharmaceutical Body' urging members to 'examine' incretin use outside serious disease. The same month, a revived fat-acceptance march draws ~20,000 in Oakland under the banner 'Full Plate'.
Lilly's retatrutide postmarketing report shows a small, dose-dependent anhedonia-scale shift. FDA declines a label change, and 'skip week' enters pharmacy-chain counselling scripts.

FDA issues a complete response letter to Amgen's monthly MariTide, requesting longer bone and body-composition data and a human-factors study. No new incretin class will reach the US market before 2033.
Year-end health-extenders package renews the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge on identical terms through 2033 and carries HRSA's incretin programme at flat $4.5B funding.

Generic semaglutide launches in the US on settlement-licensed entry dates following compound-patent expiry, with five ANDA holders and a Novo authorised generic. Cash prices fall to $39–69 a month by summer, and Lilly cuts tirzepatide's cash price to $279.

FDA approves brand semaglutide for gambling disorder under priority review, the first drug labelled for a behavioural addiction. Parity rules oblige plans to cover it, and generics carve the indication out of their labels.

open_tensions: The generic made the molecule nearly free, but not the muscle and bone monitoring. Volume is growing fastest in the unmonitored cheap-generic cohort the sarcopenia and fracture labels warn about, and the Bridge's counselling visit is the only federal check.

The gambling-disorder label sits on the brand while plans steer patients to carved-out generics. An induced-infringement suit by Novo, or a payer revolt, could decide who controls the compulsion indications. Off-label use for shopping, screens and sex is spreading without trials.

The backlash is real but politically incoherent: pastors, fat-acceptance activists, 'natural' parents and the betting industry all oppose medicated appetite for different reasons. In an election year it could become policy, aimed at pediatric use or HRSA renewal, or it could fade.

Reward blunting is now an approved therapeutic mechanism for gambling and alcohol, a mainstream complaint and a reason for skip-week self-titration. Nobody has measured what intermittent dosing does to efficacy, regain or bone.
still_true: Wegovy's brand list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Retatrutide still lists at $1,499 a month, is supply-allocated, has no TrumpRx cash price, and carries its bone and body-composition monitoring section.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
The ACA preventive mandate still covers semaglutide for smoking cessation at two 90-day courses a year, and HRSA programme sites still require only refill pickup, not weigh-ins.

prose.headline: $49, Prescribed for the Slots, Refused in the Pews: The Shot Goes Generic and 60 Million Americans Take It Anyway
prose.world_in_600_words:
In January 2032 the drug that remade American bodies became cheap. Semaglutide's patent ran out, settlement dates came due, and five generic makers launched alongside Novo Nordisk's own authorised generic. By summer a month of injectable semaglutide costs between thirty-nine and sixty-nine dollars at a chain pharmacy. Lilly cut tirzepatide to $279 to keep its patients. Wegovy's list price is still $1,349 and retatrutide's is still $1,499, still rationed, but those figures now describe a luxury tier, not the market.

About sixty million adults, more than one in five, are on an incretin. The growth came mostly from the bottom third of incomes, where use rose from thirteen to seventeen and a half percent. People who had been buying compounded vials from telehealth sites, or getting through a free ninety-day quit course, moved to a pen from the pharmacy counter. The gray market halved. What remains is research-grade retatrutide sold in gyms, a habit of ordering Indian pens by mail, and a few 'microdose' sellers. Who pays did not change. Medicare's Bridge was extended on the same terms, the federal free-clinic programme was carried at the same funding, and employers kept their exclusions or added generic-only tiers. With a cheaper drug, the same dollars cover more people. Access is no longer a question of price. It is a question of whether someone has forty-nine dollars, a prescription and a pharmacy nearby.

In March the FDA approved brand semaglutide for gambling disorder, the first drug labelled for a behavioural addiction. Mental-health parity made plans cover it, and the plans quickly learned they could route patients to generics that leave the indication off their labels. Doctors prescribe the same drug for compulsive shopping, gaming and pornography without trials. Casinos around Shreveport and Atlantic City report locals feeding the slots less. Betting companies call it a clinical headwind.

The drug's other effect has a common name now. People call it the grey, and they manage it. Lilly's long-awaited retatrutide data showed a small, dose-dependent loss of pleasure. The FDA called that consistent with how the drug works and changed nothing. Pharmacists now ask about skip weeks as routinely as they ask about allergies. A third of long-term users say they lower or skip doses on purpose, before a wedding, a pitch or an anniversary. The 'focus' subscriptions sold as perks have lost their shine, and several employers dropped them after staff complained.

The louder change is the refusal. In June 2031 the Southern Baptist Convention asked its members to examine their use. In Tulsa, a network of about 140 churches runs fasting seasons and full potlucks as an alternative to what pastors call the pharmacy fast. The same month twenty thousand people marched in Oakland under the banner 'Full Plate', reviving a fat-acceptance movement many had thought finished. Affluent parents in Austin and Nashville sign pledges to keep their children 'unmedicated', and plus-size retail has stopped shrinking. These groups agree on little else. In an election year, candidates are asked whether they are on, and some say proudly that they are not.

The ledger has not moved. The bone, muscle and gastric risks are still established and pancreatitis is still suspected. Fifty-five thousand claims sit in Philadelphia, aimed at the brand makers because federal law shields generics. No new class of drug arrived, and the FDA sent Amgen's monthly shot back asking for bone data it does not yet have. The children on liraglutide are older, and still no one has a bone readout for them. Weight is still visible in a body, but stance is now visible too: on, off, or refusing.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Renée Thibodeaux, forty-six, works the slot floor at a riverboat casino in Bossier City. At six she does her shot in the kitchen, generic semaglutide, forty-nine dollars at the Walmart on Airline Drive, and writes 'W' on the calendar. Next week has an 'S' for skip, because her daughter's quinceañera is Saturday and she wants to taste the cake.

Her husband Dale's pen sits in the butter compartment. It's the brand box, because his plan made the paperwork say gambling disorder, though the pharmacist filled it generic. He hasn't been to the riverboat in eleven weeks. He sleeps more, and he doesn't argue about the light bill anymore. She's not sure she misses the arguing.

On the floor, the regulars are thinner, and so are the machines' totals. Her manager posts the coin-in numbers on the break-room fridge with a frowning sticky note. A woman she's known nine years tells her she's off it now. Her church in Shreveport is doing the Daniel Fast and she wants to 'feel things with the Lord'. She's bought a plate of boudin balls and is eating every one, slowly, on purpose.

At lunch Renée eats half a turkey wrap and gives the rest to Marcus from security, who is on retatrutide from a gym in Plano and whose forearms look sculpted.

At home her mother has made a pot of gumbo and refuses, as always, to measure portions. Renée eats a small bowl. Dale eats one too, says it's good, and means it a little.
